name: Valdas Dambrauskas
headline: 8 years of struggle
lowest: At 25, he moves to London to become a coach. For 8 years, he takes one odd job after another: newspaper delivery, gardening, pub work, sometimes three or four jobs at once. He coaches on the side, without landing a full-time professional post.
comeback: In 2026, after more than 20 years on the road, he leads Sabah into the Champions League, all the way to Old Trafford.
lesson: The invisible years of learning end up counting.
at25: In 2002, at 25, Valdas Dambrauskas wins 4,000 litas on the Lithuanian version of a quiz show like "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?". He uses it to move to England with his partner and become a coach.

name: Elon Musk
headline: Days away from losing everything
lowest: In 2008, SpaceX has just failed to launch its rocket three times. Tesla is on the brink of bankruptcy. Musk has put much of his fortune on the line and funding is drying up.
comeback: In December 2008, SpaceX wins a major NASA contract and Tesla secures last-minute funding. Both companies survive and keep growing.
lesson: The breaking point can come right before the turnaround.
at25: In 1996, Elon Musk is building Zip2, an online city guide for newspapers he co-founded in 1995 with his brother Kimbal. After a $3 million funding round, he becomes its chief technology officer. Compaq will buy Zip2 in 1999.

name: Nelson Mandela
headline: 27 years in prison
lowest: At 44, he is imprisoned for his fight against apartheid. He spends more than 27 years behind bars, much of it on Robben Island, and turns down several offers of conditional release.
comeback: Released in 1990, at 71, he becomes South Africa's first democratically elected president four years later.
lesson: A life is not defined by its years of confinement.
at25: In 1943 and 1944, Nelson Mandela studies law at the University of the Witwatersrand, the only Black African student, while working as a clerk at a Johannesburg law firm. At Easter 1944, he co-founds the ANC Youth League.

name: Brian Chesky
headline: In debt, almost no customers
lowest: In 2008, Airbnb is not taking off. Chesky and his co-founders pile up credit card debt. Investors turn the project down and the company has almost no activity.
comeback: To survive, they sell cereal boxes themed on the US presidential candidates. In 2009, Airbnb joins Y Combinator and sees its first signs of lasting growth.
lesson: Survive long enough to find what works.
at25: In 2006 and 2007, Brian Chesky, a 2004 industrial design graduate of RISD, is a designer at 3DID in Los Angeles, where he designs toys and medical equipment. Disappointed, he cuts back his hours in 2007. Airbnb does not exist yet.

name: Patrick and John Collison
headline: 2 years for just 50 users
lowest: In 2009, the two brothers start building Stripe. For nearly 2 years, they develop their payments infrastructure, negotiate with financial players and refine their product.
comeback: At its public launch in September 2011, Stripe has only about 50 users, according to John Collison. They keep improving the service, which goes on to become a major piece of global payments infrastructure.
lesson: Recognizing a wrong course lets you start again.
at25: Patrick, born in 1988, is 25 in 2013 and 2014: he runs Stripe, co-founded in 2010 with his brother and valued at $1.75 billion in a 2014 funding round. John, born in 1990, is 25 in 2015 and 2016: he is president of Stripe, which launches Atlas in February 2016.

name: Leo XIV (Robert Prevost)
headline: Priest in Peru at 40, pope at 69
lowest: At 40, Robert Prevost lives in Peru, where he trains future priests and holds pastoral responsibilities. For many years, he works far from the Vatican's highest offices.
comeback: He becomes a bishop at 59, a cardinal at 68, and is elected pope on May 8, 2025, at 69.
lesson: A long life in the field can lead to the top.
at25: In 1980 and 1981, Robert Prevost, an Augustinian friar since 1978, studies theology at the Catholic Theological Union in Chicago. He takes his solemn vows on August 29, 1981 and will be ordained a priest in Rome in 1982.

name: José Hernández
headline: Rejected 11 times by NASA
lowest: The child of Mexican migrant farmworkers, he works in California's fields between schools. After becoming an engineer, he applies to be an astronaut and is turned down by NASA eleven times in a row.
comeback: In May 2004, on his twelfth application, he is selected for NASA Astronaut Group 19. On August 28, 2009, he flies aboard the space shuttle Discovery (mission STS-128) to the International Space Station.
lesson: Eleven rejections do not decide the twelfth.
at25: In 1987, José Hernández, who earned a master's degree from the University of California, Santa Barbara in 1986, joins Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory as an electrical engineer (signal and image processing). NASA will not select him until 2004.

name: Margaret Thatcher
headline: Grocer's daughter, Prime Minister
lowest: She grows up in a flat above the family grocery in the small town of Grantham. After studying chemistry, she tries to enter Parliament but loses the 1950 and 1951 elections.
comeback: Elected an MP in 1959, she keeps rising for twenty years. In 1979, at 53, she becomes the UK's first woman Prime Minister and stays in power for more than 11 years.
lesson: Record unpopularity does not necessarily end a career.
image_credit: Margaret Thatcher Foundation (recadrage : Begoon), Libre de droits (Copyrighted free use)
at25: In 1950 and 1951, Margaret Roberts, the future Thatcher, is a chemist at J. Lyons and Co. in Hammersmith and lives in Dartford, where she is the Conservative candidate. Beaten in February 1950, she runs again in October 1951 and loses again.

name: Jensen Huang
headline: Close to running out of cash
lowest: Nvidia's first chip, the NV1 (1995), flops: its quadrilateral rendering is incompatible with Direct3D, and Sega drops it for its next console. With the company close to running out of cash, Jensen Huang lays off more than half the staff in 1996 (from about 100 to 40).
comeback: Launched in August 1997 with about a month of payroll left, the RIVA 128 sells around a million units in four months and saves the company. Nvidia then introduces the GeForce 256 GPU in 1999, and its chips go on to power the AI boom, making it the leader in AI computing.
lesson: Admitting a mistake can save the project.
at25: In 1988, Jensen Huang is an engineer at LSI Logic in Silicon Valley, after a first job designing microprocessors at AMD. He studies at night for a master's in electrical engineering from Stanford (1992) and will co-found Nvidia in 1993.

name: Robert Downey Jr.
headline: From prison to Iron Man
lowest: Arrested in June 1996 with heroin, cocaine and a gun, he relapses again and again. In 1999, he is sentenced to three years at Corcoran state prison and his career seems ruined. After another arrest in 2001, he is fired from Ally McBeal.
comeback: Sober, he lands the role of Tony Stark in Iron Man, released on May 2, 2008, which relaunches his career. In March 2024, he wins the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for Oppenheimer.
at25: In 1990, Robert Downey Jr. is a working Hollywood actor, known for Less Than Zero (1987). He co-stars with Mel Gibson in Air America (1990), and two years later earns his first Oscar nomination for Chaplin (1992).

name: Walt Disney
headline: Bankrupt at 21, then built Disney
lowest: In 1923, at 21, his Kansas City cartoon studio Laugh-O-Gram goes bankrupt. He leaves for Hollywood that summer with little but an unfinished reel. In February 1928, he loses Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, whose rights belong to Universal, and most of his animators.
comeback: On October 16, 1923, a deal to distribute his Alice Comedies marks the start of the Disney company, run with his brother Roy. Mickey Mouse stars in Steamboat Willie on November 18, 1928, Snow White opens on December 21, 1937, and Disneyland on July 17, 1955.
image_credit: Boy Scouts of America, Public domain
at25: In 1927, Walt Disney runs his studio on Hyperion Avenue in Los Angeles with his brother Roy. After the Alice Comedies end in July, he and Ub Iwerks create Oswald the Lucky Rabbit for Universal; Trolley Troubles is released on September 5, 1927.

name: Henry Ford
headline: Two failed car companies before Ford
lowest: His Detroit Automobile Company, founded in 1899, folds in 1901; in 1902 he leaves the Henry Ford Company, which becomes Cadillac.
comeback: He founds Ford Motor Company on June 16, 1903. The Model T arrives in 1908, then the moving assembly line in 1913.
lesson: A failed start is not the end.
at25: Married to Clara Bryant in April 1888, he runs a lumber business on his father's former farmland.
